_note: SINGLE SOURCE for legitimate x86_64<->vax shippable-image differences (rd vms-e1d, INV-LEDGER). Read by tools/parity/image_parity.py. Every entry names the image(s) that legitimately exist on only ONE arch, which side lacks them, and WHY -- the reviewed record of 'why this arch legitimately differs'. A gap NOT listed here is real drift and fails the gate. Do not add an entry just to make the gate pass -- each one needs sign-off that the difference is a deliberate design choice (usually 'Decision A', vms-42d: VAX activates images via NetBSD's own ld.elf_so instead of the custom IMGACT.EXE symbol-vector scheme x86_64 uses), not an unbuilt gap.

entries.reason: Decision A (vms-42d): VAX boot images (STARTUP/PROVISION/DCL/JOB_CONTROL/LOGINOUT.EXE) are ordinary dynamic NetBSD elf32-vax executables activated by the OS's own ld.elf_so, not IMGACT.EXE's .vms$sv symbol-vector scheme -- so VAX never links against OVMX's own DECC$SHR/LIBVMS*$SHR shareable-image family, which exists only under the x86_64 VMS-native LINK.EXE activation model (docs/design-link-native-toolchain.md).

Decision A (vms-42d): VAX activates images via NetBSD's native ld.elf_so, not a custom activator, so IMGACT.EXE (the freestanding symbol-vector image activator, vms-913.11) has no VAX role by design -- not an unbuilt gap.

Decision A (vms-42d), vms-707/vms-431: RC3.EXE is the minimal RUN target for the x86_64 DCL $STATUS-propagation acceptance gate (tests/qemu/test_run_status_e2e.sh). It is a LINK.EXE-built VMS-native image (zero DT_NEEDED/DT_HASH, PT_INTERP=IMGACT.EXE) staged into SYS$SYSTEM: so `RUN SYS$SYSTEM:RC3.EXE` exercises the reworked IMGACT.EXE-over-ACP RUN fork/waitid-peek/getexit path -- the SAME custom symbol-vector activation model as IMGACT.EXE itself (already allowlisted just above). VAX activates images through NetBSD's own ld.elf_so, so a VAX build of RC3.EXE would be a different artifact testing a different activation path, and no VAX test references it (RC3 appears only under tests/qemu/). RC3.EXE therefore has no VAX role by design, exactly like its activator -- not an unbuilt gap.

Decision A (vms-42d), vms-992e: LINK.EXE is the OVMX-native linker (src/vmslink) that emits the x86_64 VMS-native image format -- ET_DYN with a .vms$sv symbol vector and zero DT_NEEDED/DT_HASH, activated by IMGACT.EXE (already allowlisted above). Its CMake target `vmslink` is added only `if(NOT NetBSD)` (CMakeLists.txt), because on VAX images are ordinary elf32-vax executables linked by NetBSD's own toolchain and activated by ld.elf_so -- there is no OVMX-native LINK.EXE role on VAX by design, the same Decision-A split as the shareable-image family and IMGACT.EXE. Not an unbuilt gap.

vms-992e: TCC.EXE is the OVMX-native C compiler (vendored tinycc, built by tests/toolchain/mk_tcc_static.sh). tinycc has NO VAX code generator (its backends are i386/x86_64/arm/arm64/riscv64 only -- there is no elf32-vax target in third-party/tcc), so a VAX TCC.EXE is not buildable at all; the VAX self-host/build story goes through the NetBSD-hosted toolchain, not a VMS-native TCC. Host-arch-only compiler by the upstream compiler's own backend support -- not an unbuilt OVMX gap.

Decision A (vms-42d), vms-fc2: MMK.EXE is the OVMX-native descrip.mms build driver (BUILD.COM's replacement, vms-e49). It orchestrates the VMS-native compile+link+activate chain -- it drives TCC.EXE then LINK.EXE (the x86_64-only VMS-native linker, already allowlisted above) and the produced image is activated by IMGACT.EXE's .vms$sv symbol-vector scheme. That whole chain is the x86_64 self-host-on-OVMX model; VAX is built through the NetBSD-hosted cross toolchain (tools/cross-vax/*.sh + NetBSD make/ld), which has no VMS-native LINK.EXE or IMGACT for MMK to drive -- so a VAX MMK.EXE has nothing to orchestrate and no VAX role by design, exactly like its LINK.EXE. Not an unbuilt gap: the VAX build story is deliberately NetBSD-hosted, not MMK-driven.

x86_64 ships the OVMX executive module as a loadable vms.ko (Linux kernel-module convention). The logically-same module ships for VAX only as vms.kmod.o (see the companion 'executive-module-packaging-vax' entry) -- NetBSD/vax GENERIC has no MODULAR framework yet (that is R3/R4 territory: tools/cross-vax/build-vax-modular-kernel.sh, the nightly netbsd-vax-devvms/netbsd-vax-boot jobs), so it cannot be a loadable .kmod today. Same module, different packaging maturity, tracked openly in tools/cut-release-vax.sh's own 'BUILD-ONLY, never a runtime claim' note -- not hidden.

Companion to 'executive-module-packaging-x86_64': x86_64 has no relocatable vms.kmod.o because its executive module ships loadable (vms.ko) directly -- there is no intermediate relocatable-object packaging step on the Linux side.
